title: The Wave Taller Than the Empire State Building
description:
Unreal but true: a new real event every day at 5:48 pm (Riyadh).

On July 9, 1958, a magnitude 7.8 earthquake shook Lituya Bay, Alaska. About 30 million cubic metres of rock fell into the narrow bay, and the splash sent water surging up the opposite mountainside. It stripped the trees and soil up to 524 metres (1,720 feet) above the water: the highest wave run-up ever documented. The Empire State Building is 443 metres to its tip.

Five people died that night. Howard Ulrich and his 7-year-old son rode over the wave in their fishing boat and survived.

The 524 m figure is how high the water climbed the slope, not the height of the wave in open water.

Sources: Alaska Earthquake Center, "60 years ago: The 1958 earthquake and Lituya Bay megatsunami" (earthquake.alaska.edu); Wikipedia, "1958 Lituya Bay earthquake and megatsunami" (citing D. J. Miller, USGS Professional Paper 354-C, 1960). Ruler heights: Statue of Liberty 93 m, Great Pyramid 139 m, Golden Gate Bridge tower 227 m, Eiffel Tower 330 m, Empire State Building 443 m.
Animation drawn in code; narration is AI-generated (ElevenLabs).

Did you guess it? Tell me your number in the comments.
